summary: If someone sells a field of a beis kor, deep holes or tall rocks in it do not count as part of the size. But if he said it is about a beis kor, they do count.

chunks.en: Someone who says to his friend,
chunks.st: If one says to another:

chunks.he: בֵּית כּוֹר עָפָר אֲנִי מוֹכֵר לְךָ,
chunks.en: I am selling you a beis kor of land,
chunks.st: I am selling you a plot of earth of the size required for sowing one kor of seed [beit kor],

words.note: A beis kor is land big enough to plant a kor of seed.

chunks.he: הָיוּ שָׁם נְקָעִים עֲמֻקִּים עֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים
chunks.en: and there were holes ten tefachim deep there
chunks.st: and there on that plot there were crevices [neka’im] ten handbreadths deep

chunks.en: or rocks ten tefachim high,
chunks.st: or rocks ten handbreadths high,

chunks.en: they are not measured with it.
chunks.explain: The buyer gets a full beis kor without them.
chunks.st: they are not measured together with
chunks.stMore: the rest of the field. Rather, the buyer must be provided with land measuring a beit kor exclusive of those crevices or rocks.

chunks.en: Less than that,
chunks.st: If the crevices or rocks measured less than ten handbreadths,

chunks.en: they are measured with it.
chunks.st: they are measured together with the rest of the field.

chunks.he: וְאִם אָמַר לוֹ כְּבֵית כּוֹר עָפָר,
chunks.en: But if he said to him, About a beis kor of land,
chunks.st: But if the seller said to the buyer: I am selling you a plot of earth that is about the size of a beit kor,

chunks.en: even if there were holes deeper
chunks.st: then even if there on that plot there were crevices deeper

chunks.en: than ten tefachim,
chunks.st: than ten handbreadths

chunks.he: אוֹ סְלָעִים גְּבוֹהִין יוֹתֵר מֵעֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים,
chunks.en: or rocks higher than ten tefachim,
chunks.st: or rocks higher than ten handbreadths,

chunks.en: they are measured with it.
chunks.st: they are measured together with the rest of the field.

summary: If a seller promised an exact size measured with a rope, any amount too little or too much must be paid back. If he said more or less, a small difference is fine, but a bigger one must be fixed with money, or sometimes by giving back land.

chunks.he: בֵּית כּוֹר עָפָר אֲנִי מוֹכֵר לְךָ
chunks.en: I am selling you a beis kor of land,
chunks.st: If one says to another: I am selling you a plot of earth the size of a beit kor,

chunks.en: measured with a rope:
chunks.st: measured precisely with a rope,

chunks.en: if it was even a little less, he takes off from the price.
chunks.st: and he gave him even the slightest amount less than what was stipulated, the seller must deduct
chunks.stMore: the difference from the purchase price of the field and return money to the buyer.

chunks.en: If it was even a little more, the buyer gives it back.
chunks.st: If he gave him even the slightest amount more than what was stipulated, the buyer must return the difference to the seller.

chunks.he: אִם אָמַר, הֵן חָסֵר הֵן יָתֵר,
chunks.en: If he said, Whether less or more,
chunks.st: And if the seller said to the buyer that he is selling him a beit kor of land more or less,

chunks.en: even if it was a quarter kav less for each se'ah,
chunks.st: then even if he gave him a quarter-kav per se’a less than what was stipulated,

chunks.en: or a quarter kav more for each se'ah, it is his.
chunks.st: or he gave him a quarter-kav per se’a more that what was stipulated, i.e., he gave him one twenty-fourth more or less than what was required, it is his.
chunks.stMore: The sale is valid, since the seller told the buyer in advance that he was not committing himself to precise measurements.

chunks.en: More than this, they make a reckoning.
chunks.st: If the difference is greater than that amount, he must make a calculation,
chunks.stMore: and the party that suffered a loss must be compensated. If the buyer received too much land, so that he must now compensate the seller,

chunks.en: What does he give back to him? Money.
chunks.st: what does he return to him? He returns money,
chunks.stMore: i.e., he pays the seller for the surplus land.

chunks.en: And if he wants, he gives him back land.
chunks.st: And if the seller so wishes, the buyer returns the surplus land to him.

chunks.en: And why did they say he gives back money?
chunks.st: Why then did the Sages say that he returns money to him?

chunks.en: To make the seller's rights stronger.
chunks.explain: The seller can ask for money instead of a small piece of land.
chunks.st: They said this in order to enhance the power of the seller,
chunks.stMore: and enable him to demand payment for the surplus land, rather than accept its return.

chunks.he: שֶׁאִם שִׁיֵּר בַּשָּׂדֶה בֵּית תִּשְׁעָה קַבִּין
chunks.en: Because if the extra in a field was room for nine kav,
chunks.st: As, if the surplus in the field was an area required for sowing nine kav of seed,

chunks.en: and in a garden room for half a kav,
chunks.st: and in a garden an area required for sowing a half-kav of seed,

chunks.en: or, as Rabbi Akiva says, a quarter kav,
chunks.st: or, according to the statement of Rabbi Akiva, an area required for sowing a quarter-kav of seed (see 11a),

chunks.en: he gives him back the land.
chunks.st: the buyer must return the land itself to the seller,
chunks.stMore: and the seller cannot demand payment in money.

chunks.he: וְלֹא אֶת הָרֹבַע בִּלְבַד הוּא מַחֲזִיר,
chunks.en: And he does not give back only the quarter kav,
chunks.st: And if the surplus is greater than a quarter-kav per se’a, it is not only the quarter-kav that he returns; rather,

chunks.en: but all of the extra.
chunks.st: he returns all of the surplus.
chunks.stMore: Since he is already required to make a refund, the refund must be made in the precise amount.

summary: If a seller uses two opposite words, like exact and more or less, Ben Nanas says we follow the last thing he said. If he sold a field by its borders, a small difference in size does not matter, but a bigger one must be paid back.

chunks.en: I am selling you an exact rope measure,
chunks.st: If the seller says to the buyer: I am selling you a plot of land of a certain size measured precisely with a rope

chunks.en: whether less or more:
chunks.st: more or less,
chunks.stMore: thereby attaching to the sale two contradictory stipulations;

chunks.en: whether less or more cancels
chunks.st: in this case, the words: More or less, nullify the words:

chunks.en: exact rope measure.
chunks.st: Measured precisely with a rope.
chunks.stMore: Accordingly, if the surplus did not exceed a quarter-kav per se’a, the sale is valid as is. Similarly, if the seller says to the buyer: I am selling you a plot of land of a certain size

chunks.he: הֵן חָסֵר הֵן יָתֵר מִדָּה בַחֶבֶל,
chunks.en: Whether less or more, exact rope measure:
chunks.st: more or less measured precisely with a rope,

chunks.en: exact rope measure cancels
chunks.st: the words: Measured precisely with a rope, nullify

chunks.en: whether less or more.
chunks.explain: We follow the last thing he said.
chunks.st: the words: More or less,
chunks.stMore: since the principle is that in all cases, one should attend to the final expression;

chunks.en: These are the words of Ben Nanas.
chunks.st: this is the statement of ben Nanas.
chunks.stMore: If one sells a field to another, telling him that he is selling him a field measuring a beit kor,

chunks.en: If he sold it with its signs and borders:
chunks.st: with its particular demarcations and borders
chunks.stMore: that the seller specifies for the buyer, the field’s measurement is not treated in as exacting a manner as in a standard sale. Therefore, if it later turns out that the field was not precisely a beit kor, but the difference is still

chunks.en: less than a sixth off, it is his.
chunks.st: less than one-sixth, the field is the buyer’s, and the sale is valid as is.
chunks.stMore: But if the difference is greater, e.g., one-quarter or one-fifth, then,

chunks.en: Up to a sixth, he takes off from the price.
chunks.st: until it is calculated at one-sixth, the seller must deduct
chunks.stMore: the difference from the purchase price and return money to the buyer.

summary: If someone sells half a field, the field is divided fairly and the buyer gets his half. If he sells the southern half, the buyer gets that half, but must give up some land for the fence and ditches between them.

chunks.he: הָאוֹמֵר לַחֲבֵרוֹ חֲצִי שָׂדֶה אֲנִי מוֹכֵר לְךָ,
chunks.en: Someone who says to his friend, I am selling you half a field,
chunks.st: If one says to another: I am selling you half a field, without specifying which half he is selling,

chunks.en: they judge the value between them, and he takes half of his field.
chunks.st: an assessment is made of the field, which is then divided between them, and the buyer takes half of the seller’s field.

chunks.en: I am selling you its southern half,
chunks.st: If the seller says: I am selling you the half that is on the southern side of the field,

chunks.en: they judge the value between them, and he takes its southern half.
chunks.st: an assessment is made of the northern and the southern sides of the field, which is then divided between them, and he takes the half on the southern side.

chunks.en: And he takes upon himself the place of the fence,
chunks.st: And he accepts upon himself to provide the space for the fence
chunks.stMore: between the two halves of the field out of his own property. He also accepts to provide out of his own property the space for the larger

chunks.en: a big ditch and a small ditch.
chunks.st: ditch and the smaller ditch,
chunks.stMore: which are meant to keep animals out of the field.

chunks.en: And how wide is a ditch?
chunks.st: And how wide is the larger ditch?

chunks.en: Six tefachim.
chunks.st: Six handbreadths.

chunks.en: And a small ditch, three.
chunks.st: And how wide is the smaller ditch? Three handbreadths.
